li.label: chosen for the new part
li.description: The council gave it to me. Soon I'll have what I lost, or near enough.

li.label: passed over for the part
li.description: There was one, and it went to someone else. I'm the one still limping.

li.label: got the part I was waiting for
li.description: There was one part, and they got it. I know it's not their fault. I still can't look at them.

li.label: fair, if hard
li.description: Their work needs it more than mine. I know that. It doesn't make the waiting easier.

li.label: chosen like a tool
li.description: The council weighed two people by what their hands are good for. That's a cold way to decide.

li.label: still waiting for a part
li.description: There's one in the stores, and it's staying there until there are two. I can wait. I'd rather not.

li.label: kept the stove
li.description: The council scrubbed the kitchen and left me at the stove. They still trust my cooking.

li.label: taken off the cooking
li.description: One bad batch, and someone else is at my stove. I'll get it back, but it stings.

li.label: trusted with the stove
li.description: The cooking is mine for a few days. I mean to do it properly.

li.label: nobody listened about the food
li.description: I spent the night sick, and the council blamed the meat and left it there.

li.label: the kitchen scrubbed
li.description: They scrubbed the kitchen from the floor up after the bad batch. I'll eat there again.

li.label: let off with a quiet word
li.description: They broke the faith's ways, and all they got was a talk by the fire. The faith deserves more than that.

li.label: the council stood against the faith
li.description: Someone broke the faith's ways, and the council stood up for them.

li.label: a penance at the altar
li.description: I spent the day scrubbing the altar on my knees, with the faithful walking past. It was meant to sting, and it did.

li.label: stitching my own wounds
li.description: I tended my own wounds with one hand and a mirror. It was the right call, and it hurt.

li.label: the best medicine for me
li.description: They opened the good medicine for me. I'll be back on my feet sooner for it.

li.label: a bad patient
li.description: Lying there telling someone else how to do my work. Every stitch, I wanted to take the needle back.

li.label: working in the cool of the night
li.description: We sleep through the worst of the heat and work under the stars. It's strange, and it's better.

li.label: a rest in the shade
li.description: When the sun is at its worst we stop and sit in the shade with water. The afternoons are bearable again.

li.label: worked through the heat
li.description: The council said carry on, so we carried on in the heat. My shirt hasn't been dry since.

li.label: let me finish it
li.description: The work is nearly done, and they let me stay at it through the night. I can see the end of it.

li.label: sent to bed when it was nearly done
li.description: I was so close, and they sent me to bed. I lay there going over it all night anyway.

li.label: a second pair of eyes
li.description: Someone sat beside me at the bench and asked good questions. It went slower, and I didn't mind.

li.label: lessons at the cell
li.description: The prisoner knows more about it than anyone I've met, and they're teaching me. Strange teacher, good lessons.

li.label: someone's sitting with the prisoner
li.description: One of ours spends an hour in the cell with the prisoner. Someone's going to get careless.

li.label: my lessons can wait
li.description: Recruit them first, the council says, and then I can learn from them. If they ever come round.

li.label: no lessons from the prisoner
li.description: The best teacher I'll ever find is sitting in a cell, and I'm not allowed near them.

li.label: the council listened about the drugs
li.description: I asked them to stop making that poison, and they did. The bench stands idle.

li.label: good silver thrown away
li.description: Traders pay well for what that bench made. Now it makes nothing.

li.label: they stopped all the drugs
li.description: Not just the hard stuff: the beer, the smoke, the lot. What's left to look forward to at night?

li.label: they kept making the drugs
li.description: I told the council what that stuff does to people, and the bench is still running.

li.label: my friend is free
li.description: The council freed my friend, and we eat at the same table now. It should always have been this way.

li.label: my friend went home
li.description: I walked my friend to the edge and watched them go. They're free, and they're gone.

li.label: my friend is still a slave
li.description: I asked for my friend's freedom, and the council said not now. Not now is a long time.

li.label: a slave set free
li.description: The council freed a slave because someone was fond of them. Our ways mean nothing, then.

li.label: the work comes first
li.description: The council didn't let it take the day from the work that needed doing. That's sense.

li.label: kept back for the cold months
li.description: The council kept back what we'll need when it's cold. Better a plain night now than a hungry one later.

li.label: no fuss made
li.description: The council let it be, and nobody had to sit through a fuss over it. Good.

li.label: one good dance
li.description: Just the one dance after the harvest, and a good one. Then bed, with the tune still going round my head.

li.label: an evening swim
li.description: Work first, then the water, still warm from the day. We stayed in until the first stars.

li.label: spring cleaning
li.description: A whole day of brooms and buckets, then a toast in a clean room. The place feels new.

li.label: everything in its place
li.description: The whole colony cleaned and put away, all at once. I could weep.

li.label: no spring cleaning
li.description: Winter's dirt is still in every corner, and the council says not this year.

li.label: walked the bounds
li.description: We walked round the edge of the colony together and stopped at every turn. I know where our land ends now.

li.label: left out of the bounds walk
li.description: The grown-ups walked the edge of the land without us.

li.label: a night under the stars
li.description: We sat out late on a warm night and looked up until our necks ached. Somebody named every star wrong.

li.label: the fishing match
li.description: An afternoon at the water with a line in, and fish for supper after. Nobody agrees who won.

li.label: the autumn hunt
li.description: The hunters went out together before the cold, and we ate well that night.

li.label: told the bees
li.description: We went from hive to hive and told the bees our news. It's an old custom, and it felt right.

li.label: the bees weren't told
li.description: Nobody went to tell the bees. It's only a custom, I know.
